correctness.rationale: Cioabă–Mim Theorems 3.8 and 3.12 supply the required homology result for order at least five. A triangle not contained in a line uses all three edge directions and after translation has vertices (0,0),(u,0),(0,u) with u≠0. The only possible fourth vertex is (u,u), possible exactly for 2u=0; no fifth is possible. This gives n²(n−1) non-line triangles and (|A[2]|−1)n²/4 intercalates, hence the stated identity trace. For a translation of order d, q whole vertex orbits in an invariant simplex contribute sign (−1)^(q−1) to the Lefschetz sum. Outside the line directions, even a single orbit fails the clique test. In a line direction each of the n preserved lines contributes 1. An invariant triangle would require order 3 and would itself be a single orbit on a line, so there are no non-line invariant triangles. The only extra faces are the n²/4 intercalates stabilized by a given line involution, each with two swaps and contribution −1 in degree three. The augmentation contributes −1. These reduced Lefschetz numbers all equal the H₂ traces. Barycentric subdivision orders each simplex by its face dimensions and removes inversions; the quotient cellular chains are coinvariants, and rational averaging is exact. Averaging the four trace cases gives the h_i,e_i formula and n−|A[2]| for H=T. The supplied finite logs were inspected but not rerun; they do not attest to the universal formulas.
